page: Vultr vc2-6c-16gb is a Cloud Compute virtual server featuring 6 vCPUs mapped to 3 physical Intel Xeon cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance utilizes a shared CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding 2.67 GB of RAM per core, and includes 320 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU hardware is present on this instance.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the shared CPU architecture results in lower-tier single-core execution. Stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores fall within the bottom 25% and bottom 10% respectively. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels in stress-ng tests, though Geekbench multi-core and Passmark CPU scores remain in the weak category. Memory read bandwidth is average at 407.68 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 48.31 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, but large block write bandwidth is weak at 18.72 GB/sec. Text processing, compression, and decompression tasks show poor performance, while ray tracing and extended instruction tests reach average tiers.

This server offers a high local storage capacity of 320 GB NVMe SSD relative to its shared CPU resources, presenting a cost-efficient option for storage-heavy workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance. Due to the shared CPU allocation and weak single-core metrics, it is not suited for intensive real-time processing or heavy database operations, as reflected in its weak Passmark database and Redis SET benchmarks. It is best suited for general-purpose utility workloads, basic web serving, development environments, and lightweight multi-threaded applications that benefit from local NVMe storage without demanding continuous high-frequency compute power.
